identity.title: A Hot Molecular Circumstellar Disk around the Massive Protostar Orion Source I

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report new Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of a circumstellar disk around Source I in Orion KL, an archetype of massive protostar candidate.

question.value: Do submillimeter H2O lines, including a vibrationally excited line, trace a hot rotating circumstellar disk around the massive protostar Source I, and what are its mass and temperature?

evidence.quote: The present results provide a further evidence of hot and neutral circumstellar disk rotating around Source I with a diameter of $\sim$100 AU scale.
This letter makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00199.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows, 468.750 MHz each, 122 kHz channel spacing

evidence.quote: The ALMA correlator provided four spectral windows with a bandwidth of 468.750 MHz for each. The channel spacing of spectrometers was 122 kHz.
336.227931 GHz ($\nu_{2}=1, 5_2,3$-$6_{1,6}$) were observed simultaneously.
The array was consisted of 21-28 antennas with a diameter of 12 m each
in the extended configuration with the maximum baseline length of 400 m.
The resultant beam size is 0.40$''$$\times$0.34$''$  with a position angle of 60 degrees.
The image rms noise level was $\sim$30 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at each channel.
The on-source integration time was about 100 seconds for each session.
Observations were carried out with ALMA on July 16, August 25, and October 21, 2012.

what.value: H2O lower state energy levels (1846 K and 2939 K)

evidence.quote: The lower state energy levels are 1846 K and 2939 K for the 321 GHz and 336 GHz H$_{2}$O lines, respectively (cite: Chen2000).

what.value: Tracking position of bursting 22 GHz H2O maser

evidence.quote: the tracking center position was taken to be the bursting 22 GHz H$_{2}$O maser
A primary flux calibrator, band-pass calibrator, and secondary gain calibrator were Callisto, J053851-440507/J0423-013, and J0607-085, respectively.
we estimated an accuracy of flux measurements to be $\sim$20%.

self_calibration.value: Phase and amplitude self-cal on Orion KL continuum from line-free channels, applied to all channels

evidence.quote: First, both phase and amplitude self-calibrations were done with the continuum emission of Orion KL by integrating over line-free channels.

task.value: CASA synthesis imaging, velocity resolution 0.125 km/s

evidence.quote: We set a velocity resolution of 0.125 km s$^{-1}$ (corresponds to 130-140 kHz resolution) in the synthesized imaging of the H$_{2}$O lines.
by using the uniform-weighted visibility data with a UV distance longer than 200 k$\lambda$.

method.value: Self-calibration on continuum, applied to lines; uniform-weighted imaging with uv > 200 kλ

evidence.quote: The solutions of self-calibration were applied to all the spectral channels including the target H$_{2}$O lines.

validation.value: Compared continuum and methyl formate lines across sessions to check flux stability

evidence.quote: We compared the continuum emission and selected spectral lines of methyl formate, HCOOCH$_{3}$ to check the stability of the observed flux scale.

method.value: 2D Gaussian fitting to velocity channel maps to find peak positions

evidence.quote: we made velocity centroid maps (peak positions of velocity channel maps) of both lines by performing two dimensional Gaussian fitting to the synthesized images.
Formal errors in the Gaussian fitting, 0.005-0.02$''$ (1$\sigma$), are almost consistent with this expectation.

validation.value: Compared with SiO maser maps and VLBI

evidence.quote: The resemblance of 321 GHz H$_{2}$O emission and previous vibrationally-excited SiO maser observations ensures that the distribution of the H$_{2}$O emission traced by ALMA is reliable

method.value: Linear velocity gradient of edge-on rotating ring

evidence.quote: If we simply assume a linear velocity gradient of the rotating edge-on ring with a radius of 42 AU, the enclosed mass is estimated to be 5$M_{\odot}$.
Because of its proximity to the Sun at a distance of 420 pc (cite: Menten2007; Kim2008), Orion KL (Kleinman-Low object) has been recognized as one of the best laboratories

analysis_steps.goal: Edge-on ring model of PV diagram and spectrum

method.value: Grid of ring inner/outer radii (rin 5-55 AU, rout 40-60 AU), Mrot 7 and 10 Msun, uniform temperature/density; compare to PV diagram and spectral profile

evidence.quote: we calculated models for several parameter set of inner and outer radii of the ring, $r_{\mbox{in}}$=5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55 AU and $r_{\mbox{out}}$=40, 50, and 60 AU

key_parameters.value: Best model rin=45 AU, rout=50 AU, Mrot=7 Msun

evidence.quote: the model with $r_{\mbox{in}}$=45 AU and $r_{\mbox{out}}$=50 AU is found to well reproduce the observed PV diagram and spectral profile
a uniform H$_{2}$O density of 5$\times$10$^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$

fitting.value: Visual comparison of model spectrum to observed profile; Tex > 3000 K

evidence.quote: we estimate the excitation temperature of the 336 GHz H$_{2}$O line, $T_{\mbox{ex}}$, by fitting the observed line profile
what we have done is a proof-of-concept model calculation
Synthesis imaging and self-calibration were done with the CASA software package.
the enclosed mass is estimated to be 5$M_{\odot}$
a slightly larger radius of 47 AU yields a consistent value of 7$M_{\odot}$
can be reconciled with an excitation temperature of $>$3000 K
Peak intensity and rms noise level of the continuum emission are 698 mJy beam$^{-1}$ and 9 mJy beam$^{-1}$, respectively.

findings_qualitative.value: First detection of the vibrationally excited 336 GHz H2O line in a star-forming region; 321 GHz map follows the outflow base like SiO masers, 336 GHz traces the disk midplane

evidence.quote: Thus, this is the first detection of the 336 GHz H$_{2}$O line in star-forming regions.

claims.hypothesis: The 336 GHz H2O line traces a hot rotating disk around Source I
claims.experiment: Centroid maps, PV diagram and ring model of the 336 GHz line
claims.result: Velocity gradient perpendicular to outflow; ring model with M>7 Msun, Tex>3000 K fits
claims.finding: Hot neutral circumstellar disk of ~100 AU rotates around Source I

evidence.quote: We detected a hot neutral circumstellar disk rotating around Source I with a scale of 100 AU in diameter.

claims.hypothesis: The 321 GHz line traces the same structure as vibrationally excited SiO masers
claims.experiment: Compare centroid map with SiO maser maps
claims.result: Inverted Z-shaped structure similar to SiO
claims.finding: Both trace the outflow base from the disk surface

evidence.quote: Thus, the vibrationally-excited SiO masers and the 321 GHz H$_{2}$O line trace the same dynamical structure

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: NW-SE outflow rejected: would need ~20 km/s expansion giving proper motion inconsistent with stable 43 GHz continuum

evidence.quote: which is inconsistent with a stable structure of the 43 GHz continuum emission (cite: Goddi2011).

limitations_admitted.value: Parameters degenerate and uncertain with single transition at limited resolution

evidence.quote: it is hard to solve a degeneracy of disk parameters, such as mass, size, and temperature

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass and Tex rely on a simple uniform ring with no formal fit or uncertainties
Possible maser excitation of 336 GHz line not excluded

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA data are public and the imaging recipe is brief, but the model code and many parameters are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The model is not fully specified and has no formal fit.
